chapter_title: Madam Rides the Bus (including 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon')

mind_map.root_topic: Chapter 7: Independence, Initiation into Life/Death & True Heroism

branches.theme: Prose Narrative: Madam Rides the Bus by Vallikkannan

details: 8-year-old Valli's strongest desire is to ride the bus running between her village and the nearest town (6 miles away).
Calculates logistics: 30 paise fare one way (60 paise round trip), 45 minutes trip duration.
Saves 60 paise by denying herself peppermints, toys, and merry-go-round rides at the fair.
Schedules journey during her mother's 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM afternoon nap.
evidence_or_examples: Refusing merry-go-round ride despite having a coin to save full 60 paise.

sub_branches.concept: The Bus Journey and Independent Persona
details: Boards the 1:00 PM bus independently; proudly rejects help from the conductor, who humorously calls her 'Madam'.
Stands on her seat to enjoy views of green fields, palm trees, and mountains.
Laughs heartily at a young cow running frantically in front of the bus.
evidence_or_examples: Conductor teasing: 'Don't be angry with me, fine conductor... Mind, Madam, step this way.'

details: In town, Valli stays in her seat and pays 30 paise for the return journey.
On the return trip, she sees the same cow lying dead on the roadside, struck by a fast vehicle.
The sudden sight of death extinguishes her joy, teaching her her first sobering lesson about mortality and life's fragility.
evidence_or_examples: Valli sitting silently, no longer looking out the window on the return trip.

branches.theme: Poetic Study: The Tale of Custard the Dragon by Ogden Nash

sub_branches.concept: Subversion of Heroism in Comic Ballad
details: Belinda lives with pets who boast of courage: Ink (kitten) and Blink (mouse) chase lions down stairs; Mustard (dog) is brave as a enraged tiger; Custard (dragon) cries for a safe cage.
An armed pirate attacks the house; all boastful pets panic and flee.
Custard steps up, snorts like an engine, clashes his tail like irons in a dungeon, and devours the pirate whole, proving true bravery.
evidence_or_examples: Custard charging the pirate like a robin at a worm.
